item_name: Staff Assessment of Resident Mood (PHQ-9-OV©) — J. Being short-tempered, easily annoyed

lookback_source.quote: Conduct the interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

lookback_notes: The assessor's observation/interview window for D0500 is the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD (p. D-13). A separate symptom-recall period is embedded in the item stem and frequency codes: staff are asked about the last 2 weeks ("Over the last 2 weeks, did the resident have any of the following problems or behaviors?", p. D-12; "Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred," p. D-15). The manual does not state how the 7-day window is counted relative to the ARD (e.g., ARD plus 6 prior days) on these pages.

coding_levels.label: No (Column 1, Symptom Presence)
coding_levels.definition: Symptoms listed are not present. Enter 0 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if symptoms listed are not present. Enter 0 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

coding_levels.label: Yes (Column 1, Symptom Presence)
coding_levels.definition: Symptoms listed are present. Enter 0, 1, 2, or 3 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if symptoms listed are present. Enter 0, 1, 2, or 3 in Column 2, Symptom Frequency.

coding_levels.label: Never or 1 day (Column 2, Symptom Frequency)
coding_levels.definition: Staff indicate that the resident has never or has experienced the symptom on only 1 day.

source.quote: Code 0, never or 1 day: if staff indicate that the resident has never or has experienced the symptom on only 1 day.

coding_levels.label: 2-6 days (several days) (Column 2, Symptom Frequency)
coding_levels.definition: Staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 2-6 days.

source.quote: Code 1, 2-6 days (several days): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 2-6 days.

coding_levels.label: 7-11 days (half or more of the days) (Column 2, Symptom Frequency)
coding_levels.definition: Staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 7-11 days.

source.quote: Code 2, 7-11 days (half or more of the days): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 7-11 days.

coding_levels.label: 12-14 days (nearly every day) (Column 2, Symptom Frequency)
coding_levels.definition: Staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 12-14 days.

source.quote: Code 3, 12-14 days (nearly every day): if staff indicate that the resident has experienced the symptom for 12-14 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: D0500J is item J of the Staff Assessment of Resident Mood (PHQ-9-OV©): "Being short-tempered, easily annoyed," coded in two columns (1. Symptom Presence and 2. Symptom Frequency).

source.quote: J. Being short-tempered, easily annoyed

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not conduct the Staff Assessment of Resident Mood (D0500, including J) if the Resident Mood Interview (D0150–D0160) was completed.

source.quote: Do not conduct if Resident Mood Interview (D0150–D0160) was completed

federal_coding_rules.rule: The staff assessment asks whether the resident had the problem or behavior over the last 2 weeks; if the symptom is present enter 1 (yes) in Column 1, Symptom Presence, then move to Column 2, Symptom Frequency, and indicate symptom frequency.

source.quote: Over the last 2 weeks, did the resident have any of the following problems or behaviors? If symptom is present, enter 1 (yes) in column 1, Symptom Presence. Then move to column 2, Symptom Frequency, and indicate symptom frequency.

federal_coding_rules.rule: The Staff Assessment is completed only when D0100 is coded 0, No; it is not completed based on resident performance during the Resident Mood Interview.

source.quote: The assessor will complete the Staff Assessment only when D0100 is coded 0, No. The assessor does not complete the Staff Assessment based on resident performance during the Resident Mood Interview.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not complete the Staff Assessment of Resident Mood items (D0500) if the resident interview should have been conducted but was not done, or if the assessment being completed is a stand-alone Part A PPS Discharge assessment.

source.quote: Do not complete the Staff Assessment of Resident Mood items (D0500) if the resident interview should have been conducted but was not done, or if the assessment being completed is a stand-alone Part A PPS Discharge assessment.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If symptom frequency in D0150A2 through D0150I2 is blank or dashed for 3 or more items, the resident interview is deemed not complete, D0160 is coded "99," the Staff Assessment of Mood is not completed, and the assessor skips to D0700, Social Isolation.

source.quote: If symptom frequency in items D0150A2 through D0150I2 is blank or dashed for 3 or more items, the interview is deemed NOT complete. Total Severity Score should be coded as "99," do not complete the Staff Assessment of Mood, and skip to D0700, Social Isolation.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Conduct the staff interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD, interviewing staff from all shifts who know the resident best.

source.quote: Conduct the interviews during the 7-day look-back period based on the ARD.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Encourage staff to report symptom frequency even if the staff believes the symptom to be unrelated to depression.

source.quote: Encourage staff to report symptom frequency, even if the staff believes the symptom to be unrelated to depression.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If frequency cannot be determined by staff interview because the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, talk to family or significant other and review transfer records to inform the selection of a frequency code.

source.quote: If frequency cannot be determined by staff interview because the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, talk to family or significant other and review transfer records to inform the selection of a frequency code.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred, using the descriptive and/or numeric categories on the form.

source.quote: Ask the staff member being interviewed to select how often over the past 2 weeks the symptom occurred. Use the descriptive and/or numeric categories on the form (e.g., "nearly every day" or 3 = 12-14 days) to select a frequency response.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a longer item was separated into its component parts, select the highest frequency rating that is reported.

source.quote: If you separated a longer item into its component parts, select the highest frequency rating that is reported.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the staff member has difficulty selecting between two frequency responses, code for the higher frequency.

source.quote: If the staff member has difficulty selecting between two frequency responses, code for the higher frequency.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, also talk to the family or significant other and review transfer records to inform selection of the frequency code.

source.quote: If the resident has been in the facility for less than 2 weeks, also talk to the family or significant other and review transfer records to inform selection of the frequency code.

federal_coding_rules.rule: D0500J's frequency score in Column 2 is one of the 10 items added into D0600, Total Severity Score (maximum 30); the staff interview is successfully completed if staff answered the frequency responses of at least 8 out of 10 items.

source.quote: The interview is successfully completed if the staff members were able to answer the frequency responses of at least 8 out of 10 items on the PHQ-9-OV©.

federal.criterion: Certain staff responses to D0500J (e.g., "They're OK if you know how to approach them," "They can snap but usually when their pain is bad," "Not with me," "They're irritable") are given as examples that indicate a need for follow-up questioning with the staff member before coding.

source.quote:
10. D0500J, Being Short-Tempered, Easily Annoyed
• They're OK if you know how to approach them.

federal.notes: Framed as examples of responses requiring follow-up questioning, not as required record documentation.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section D pages do not tie D0500J to any payment or case-mix classification.
